significance: Liverpool came back from 3-0 down at half-time to level and then win on penalties in the most dramatic Champions League final ever played.
Pep Guardiola's Barcelona dismantled Manchester United in Rome to complete a historic treble in his very first season as manager.
Real Madrid finally ended their 12-year wait for La Décima, scoring three times in extra time after Ramos's last-gasp header levelled it at 1-1.
Liverpool claimed their sixth European Cup in Madrid, with a Salah penalty and late Origi goal securing Klopp's first Champions League title.
Rodri's deflected strike gave Manchester City a historic treble, completing the Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League in a single season under Guardiola.
Manchester United scored twice in injury time through Sheringham and Solskjær to steal the trophy from Bayern Munich and complete an unprecedented treble.
Drogba's 88th-minute header forced extra time in Bayern's home stadium, and Chelsea won on penalties to claim the one trophy their billionaire owner had always craved.
Two city rivals met in a second final in three years, with Real Madrid winning on penalties after Sergio Ramos scored in normal time and Atlético equalised late on.
The only all-Italian Champions League final ended goalless before Shevchenko's decisive penalty gave Milan the trophy at Manchester United's Old Trafford.
Arsenal's Jens Lehmann became the first goalkeeper sent off in a Champions League final, yet the ten men held out until late before Eto'o and Belletti broke their hearts.

Without Salah or Firmino, Liverpool produced one of the greatest comebacks in football history, with Wijnaldum scoring twice and a cheeky Alexander-Arnold corner catching Barcelona completely off guard.
The first World Cup final decided by penalties ended in heartbreak for Roberto Baggio, whose decisive spot-kick sailed over the bar to hand Brazil their fourth title.
France won their first World Cup on home soil as a mysteriously ill Ronaldo started but contributed little, while Zidane headed in twice to inspire a crushing victory.
Ronaldo scored twice to exorcise the demons of 1998 and win Brazil an unprecedented fifth World Cup, silencing a tournament that had already knocked out France, Argentina and Portugal.
Zidane's final act in professional football was a headbutt on Materazzi, earning a red card in extra time before Italy converted the decisive penalty to win their fourth World Cup.
Iniesta's extra-time winner gave Spain their first ever World Cup trophy, completing a golden era of tiki-taka that also delivered back-to-back European Championships.
Götze's extra-time chest and volley ended Argentina's 24-year wait for a third title and gave Germany their fourth, cementing a generation of Bundesliga-bred talent as world champions.
France became world champions for the second time with a thrilling win that featured an own goal, a VAR penalty and a stunning Mbappé strike as Croatia's fairytale run finally ended.
Messi finally won the World Cup in a breathtaking final where Mbappé scored a hat-trick to force extra time, yet Argentina held on in the shootout to end their 36-year wait.
The Mineirazo — Germany's 7-1 demolition of host nation Brazil — was the most humiliating result in World Cup semi-final history, with five goals scored in an astonishing 18-minute spell.
Puyol's towering header gave Spain victory over Germany in the semi-final, putting the tiki-taka masters into their first ever World Cup final.
Greece produced one of the greatest upsets in football history, beating tournament hosts Portugal twice — including the final — with Charisteas's header sealing an extraordinary triumph.
Fernando Torres's clinical finish midway through the first half was enough for Spain to end their 44-year wait for a European Championship and launch a golden era of dominance.
Spain's 4-0 demolition of Italy confirmed them as the greatest international side of their generation, becoming the first team ever to win three consecutive major international tournaments.
Eder's stunning extra-time strike gave Portugal their first ever major international trophy despite Ronaldo going off injured early on, in a tournament where they'd drawn all three group games.
Italy won their first European Championship in 53 years by defeating England on penalties at Wembley, after Bonucci equalised to cancel out Luke Shaw's early opener.
Agüero's 94th-minute winner against QPR — announced by Martin Tyler's immortal commentary — gave Manchester City their first league title in 44 years on goal difference from United.

Gerrard's infamous slip let Demba Ba in for the first goal, effectively ending Liverpool's title challenge and handing the initiative to Manchester City in one of the most gut-wrenching moments in Premier League history.
Tottenham's failure to beat Chelsea confirmed Leicester City as Premier League champions at odds of 5000-1, completing the most improbable title win in the history of top-flight English football.
Pep Guardiola's Barcelona delivered the most emphatic El Clásico humiliation of the modern era, with Mourinho's Real Madrid — then second in the table — left utterly dismantled at the Camp Nou.
